description: Dynamic styling rules evaluated by RulesEngine singleton. Rules can target overlays across all cards using IDs, tags, types, or patterns.

id.description: Unique rule identifier used for debugging and tracing

name.description: A readable label for the rule (shown in the editor)

when.description: Condition(s) that must be met for rule to apply: entity state and attributes, map_range_cond, time_between, weekday_in, sun_elevation, JavaScript and Jinja2 conditions, and logical composition (all/any/not). Numeric comparisons accept above/below (strict) and at_least/at_most (inclusive).

apply.description: Style changes, animations and base SVG filters to apply when conditions are met

overlays.description: Overlay style changes using direct IDs or selectors (all, type:, tag:, pattern:, exclude:)

base_svg.description: Base SVG filter updates (MSD cards only)

filters.description: Filters to apply: a stackable filter list [{mode, type, value}] (or the legacy CSS filter object); an empty list clears them

animations.description: Animations to trigger when rule matches. Supports overlay targeting (ID, tag, type, pattern) and automatic lifecycle management (start on match, stop on unmatch).

tag.description: Target all overlays with this tag (recommended for cross-card coordination)

type.description: Target all overlays of this type

duration.description: Animation duration in milliseconds. Also accepts a map_range descriptor for entity-driven dynamic duration.

oneOf.description: true = loop infinitely, false = play once
Number of additional times to loop

loop.description: Loop animation. Automatically stops when the rule unmatches. true = infinite, N = loop N times

delay.description: Delay before animation starts (milliseconds). Also accepts a map_range descriptor for entity-driven dynamic delay.

ease.description: Animation easing function (anime.js v4 name, or an object with type and params). Simple strings like 'inOutQuad', 'outBounce', 'inElastic'.

alternate.description: Whether animation should alternate direction on each loop. Left out, the preset decides.

target.description: CSS selector for a single animation target element, or `background` to animate the card's background_animation effects (their config keys in params, with preset: custom).

targets.description: CSS selector(s) for multiple animation target elements.

effect.description: With target: background, the index of the background_animation entry to animate (0 is the first, the bottom layer). Without it, every entry.

essential_motion.description: Keep playing when the device asks for reduced motion (prefers-reduced-motion). Only for motion that carries meaning, such as an alert flash; other animations jump to their end state or stay still.

id.description: Optional identifier for this animation entry (referenced by system animations, debugging).

enabled.description: Set false to disable this animation entry without deleting it.

timeline-cascade.description: Params for the "timeline-cascade" preset: multi-step timeline. Timing/easing for each step lives in that step's own config; the top-level canonical `duration`/`ease` are genuinely inert (confirmed against anime.js's own source: Timeline recomputes its own duration from its children regardless, and `ease` isn't read by the underlying Timer class at all; only a separate `playbackEase` is). `loop`/`alternate`/`delay`, however, do still apply: they govern the whole timeline's repeat/reverse/start-delay behavior, since Timeline extends Timer and inherits those from the same top-level params.

timeline-attention.description: Params for the "timeline-attention" preset: 3-phase scale/shake/settle sequence. The top-level canonical `duration`/`ease` are genuinely inert (durations are hardcoded to the duration_* fields below, and each phase's easing is hardcoded in source with no override; confirmed via anime.js's own source that Timeline discards a top-level duration and never reads `ease` at all). Of the remaining canonical fields, only `loop` is actually forwarded by the preset factory (repeats the whole 3-phase sequence); `alternate`/`delay` are never read by this preset's code despite being generically available on the Timeline class, so they were deliberately left out of this schema.

oneOf.description: Repeats the whole 3-phase sequence.
Used to build a fixed 5-point translateX keyframe array.
Duration of phase 1 (scale up).
Duration of phase 2 (shake).
Duration of phase 3 (settle back).

params.description: Preset-specific parameters. Values may be static or use map_range to proportionally interpolate from an entity value.

stop.description: When this rule matches, lower-priority rules no longer patch the same overlays (they are still evaluated)

priority.description: Rule evaluation priority (higher values evaluated first, default: 0)

item_apply_animations_item_params_colors.description: Colour value (hex, rgb, named colour, theme token, or CSS variable)

oneOf.description: Characters shown at the reveal edge: true for '_', or a string. Best seen on slower decodes (a longer duration).
Repurposed as per-element stagger step (ms), NOT the canonical single start-offset.
Also accepted nested here (top-level wins if both set). Also accepts a map_range descriptor for entity-driven, live-adjusting duration on looping animations.
Random offset in ms added to each target's delay (plus or minus). A [start, end] pair ramps it along the stagger order.
Any number: the same random pattern on every load. Leave unset for a new pattern each time. Targets with the same seed share the pattern.

item_apply_animations_item_params_steps_.description: CSS selector (or list of selectors) for this step, resolved inside the card: in an MSD card any overlay of that card, e.g. [data-overlay-id="line_1"]. Without it the step animates the animation's own target(s).
